title: Port the midking screen entry's values onto the champion: mergeMinUnits 8->30, beaconRound 405->195, foldRound 397->200: it scores 0.55 against v0035 over 100 games
hypothesis: Screen port (loop/screenport.py, method note M24). The `midking` opponent-screen entry (referee/gauntlet.toml: d52bfb4, built on v0033, with beaconRound = 195, foldRound = 200, mergeMinUnits = 30) is 2 promotions older than the current champion v0035 (aa92d8b), yet it scored 0.550 against it over 100 games (E0132's screen, the champion as its candidate), where an entry that far behind usually loses clearly. Its points in each earlier champion's latest screen (100 games each unless stated): 38046fa 0.53 (E0132). So what its values do may be worth having in today's bot: this idea sets mergeMinUnits 8->30, beaconRound 405->195, foldRound 397->200 on the current champion and changes nothing else. Compare each param's comment in v0033's and today's params.hpp first: where its meaning changed since, port the behaviour the entry's value had, not the number. A level score says the entry keeps up despite the promotions it lacks, not that its values gain: test it alone by SPRT as usual. If the SPRT's per-opponent scores pull apart, make a value depend on something the bot can observe rather than a new constant; if it is kept, a follow-up can test which value carries it.
